title: Cylinders over H^m-null sets are H^{m+1}-null
statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and write π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^P for y = (y_0, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))). Let H^k := μHE[k] be Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure. If N ⊆ ℝ^P satisfies H^m(N) = 0, then the cylinder {y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} : π(y) ∈ N} = ℝ × N satisfies H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0. (This is verbatim Part (a), the first conjunct, of the parent theorem.)
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) N = 0 → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0
